full_caption: Kingsmere Development Partners, L.P., Appellant, v. Isolde Ingleside, Appellee
court: Ardenne District Court of Appeal, Fourth District
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Kingsmere Development Partners, L.P. and Isolde Ingleside own riparian tracts along the Sable Fork within Windmere County. The dispute concerns Isolde Ingleside's diversion of approximately 1,750 gallons per minute for irrigation of 12.5 acres.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Groundwater in this State is governed by the rule of reasonable use, under which an overlying owner may withdraw for beneficial use on the overlying land but may not export off-tract to the injury of neighboring wells.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Reasonableness is a question of fact informed by the purpose of the use, its economic and social value, the extent of the harm, the practicality of avoiding the harm, and the protection of existing investments.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The public trust doctrine reserves to the State title to the beds of navigable waters. Navigability for title purposes is determined by susceptibility to commercial navigation at the date of statehood.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Under the riparian doctrine as modified in this State, each riparian owner is entitled to a reasonable use of the watercourse, measured against the correlative rights of other riparians.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The 87 days of well failure experienced by Kingsmere Development Partners, L.P. coincided with the operation of Isolde Ingleside's high-capacity irrigation well 50 feet from the shared aquifer boundary. Causation was established by drawdown modeling.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Accretion belongs to the riparian owner; avulsion does not change the boundary. The 1990 channel shift, being sudden and perceptible, was avulsive and left the boundary at the former thread of the stream.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The injunction is modified to permit diversion not exceeding 125 gallons per minute between April and August, and is otherwise affirmed.

sections.heading: RIDER B — MINIMUM BYPASS FLOW AND MEASUREMENT
sections.text: A minimum bypass flow sufficient to satisfy downstream domestic and stock-watering needs shall be maintained at all times. Each diverting party shall install and maintain a totalizing meter at the point of diversion, shall record readings weekly, and shall furnish records to any other riparian owner within 3 days of written request. Domestic use has priority over irrigation, and irrigation over industrial use, in every period of shortage.

sections.heading: RIDER C — GROUNDWATER AND WELL INTERFERENCE
sections.text: No high-capacity well shall be completed within 50 feet of an existing domestic well without a drawdown analysis furnished to the affected owner. If operation of a high-capacity well causes an existing domestic well to fail or its yield to fall below five gallons per minute, the operator shall, at its expense, deepen or replace the affected well or provide an equivalent permanent supply. Withdrawal for export off the overlying tract is prohibited where it injures a neighboring overlying user.

sections.heading: RIDER E — BOUNDARY, ACCRETION AND PUBLIC TRUST
sections.text: Where the boundary is a watercourse, gradual accretion and reliction move the boundary with the water; a sudden and perceptible avulsive change does not, and the boundary remains at the former thread of the stream. Nothing in this instrument conveys any interest in the bed of a navigable water, title to which is held by the State in trust for the public.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Governing Law
sections.text: This instrument shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ardenne, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this instrument shall be brought exclusively in the courts sitting in Windmere County, Ardenne, and each party consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Force Majeure
sections.text: Neither party shall be liable for a failure of performance, other than an obligation to pay money, caused by an act of God, flood, fire, civil disturbance, governmental order, epidemic, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control, provided the affected party gives notice within 3 days and resumes performance as promptly as practicable.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Successors, Assigns and Runs With the Land
sections.text: The benefits and burdens created by this instrument touch and concern the subject land, are intended by the parties to run with the land in perpetuity, and bind every successor in title with notice, actual, constructive or inquiry. A conveyance of the benefited parcel carries the benefit whether or not this instrument is mentioned in the deed of conveyance.
